Q: Why Java uses PrintStream and InputStream by default for System class? A:

The short answer is that those classes (InputStream, OutputStream, PrintStream, etc) were the only ones available in Java 1.0. So that is what the System class used ... and still uses.

The Reader and Writer classes were added in 1.1, Scanner in 1.5, Console in 1.6 and so on.

Java 1.0 was rushed to market in a hurry in 1995 to meet the perceived need for a language that could run in the first web browsers. That rush meant that various aspects of the Java language and runtime were "underdone" ... and Java 1.0.x were barely usable. Later Java releases have progressively remedied nearly all of those issues, but some things could not be fixed without breaking backwards compatibility. The System.in,out,err API design is a prime example.

Q: Do SQL databases apply WHERE filters before joins? A:

No. Logically, joins happen first, then WHERE filters the result.

In practice, optimizers often push filters down before the join for performance but the logical order is always JOIN → WHERE.

Q: Pulling in an include path from within a C++ project's source A:

Before I made my library optionally header only, I was distributing a tar.gz of unmodified Eigen, and a CMakeLists that handled extracting and including the appropriate directories. In my updated approach in the comments below, I'm still redistributing the unmodified Eigen, but in extracted form. In either case, yes, there is the extra bloat you mentioned.

My reason for wanting the user to not have to worry about Eigen and just -I a single path is that the target audience is likely to be novice programmers and students, and I want the usage to be as absolutely simple as I can make it.

Q: Dashboard Setup: Same Repo or Separate Project? A:

Security through obscurity is not really security. If your actual security is doe properly then whether other users can guess the dashboard URL or not will be irrelevant.

And anyway that has nothing at all to do with whether you store the code in the same repository or not.
